For the sake of this post I'll assume that you have a basic knowledge of Freud's psychosexual stages of development. What most people (not necessarily psychologists) view Freud is a sex obsessed crazy man, I strongly believe there is some truth in his clams. In advance a warning this post is long, and to keep it relatively short I just give examples regarding two stages of the psychosexual stages of development.

Looking at the psychosexual stages of development, when one gets stuck in the oral stage (something goes wrong at this stage for example too much breastfeeding leading to a fixation at this stage), in adult life this individual would be either highly independent or dependent (doctrine of duality). Based on my personal life experience, I've met a few brave enough to talk about themselves without trying a sell a certain socially desirable image. For example I know a couple of people who are highly dependent/independent and compulsively smoke, bite their nails, like keeping things in their month (eg. chew gum all the time) enjoy more oral sex, eating, drinking and enjoy talking more; simply put have oral personalities. What I believe Freud tried to illustrate, is that there is a certain proportion of people that pass through each of the psychosexual stages of development and become a "normal" adult and there are people who get fixated at a certain stage.

To give another example, let's look at the highly controversial phallic stage. Fixation at the phallic stage results from the inability to identify with an adult, in particular with the same sex parent and according to the psychoanalytic theory the fixation can result in homosexuality, exhibitionism, impulsiveness, vanity, problems with authority and rejection of appropriate gender roles. As an adult the person is most likely viewed as "cocky" by peers. Where the link with homosexuality comes in, that a boy due to failure in identification with the father identifies more with the mother leading to acquiring more feminine behaviors and thinking patterns.

This is where research supposedly fails to support this theory, as in the UK more than 1 out of 10 children are raised by single mothers without any significant correlation to homosexuality. Research usually points the cause of homosexuality to genetic and/or biological component. But that's where I don't agree because not every single male that is raised by a single mother is stuck in the phallic stage. People mostly interpret the psychosexual development by believing everyone is ‘stuck’ at a given stage. But that's a wrong assumption, only a proportion of the population is fixated at a given stage, and there are five different stages.

I would love to see (or even be able to conduct such research without being labelled as crazy) for example in this case a study that would take a control group that was raised by single mothers that show characteristics of a person who successfully went through all the stages of psycho-sexual development and a group which represent characteristics of a phallic stage fixation that were raised by single mothers to examine whether we can actually disapprove this claim rather than just looking and the entire population. Moreover, once again I know from personal experience people that are likely to be fixated at the phallic stage, that exhibits some (but not necessarily all) expected adult characteristics and has struggled with the Oedipus complex resulting from the fixation at exactly this stage. 

As to other aspects of the phallic fixation, there is a certain logic to Freud’s idea that you become vain, impulsive and exhibitionistic because when you masturbate as a child, you don’t get told enough that you can’t do that so you grow up feeling you can do anything. Certainly those high on the temperamental dimension of psychoticism would express themselves unrestrainedly if not taught through operant conditioning that certain things were not acceptable. Social Learning Theory could be implicated here in that we model the impulsive and compulsive behavior of others - particularly if the RED vMEME saw that kind of behavior as a short-cut to getting what it wants.

The trouble that lies with the psychosexual stages of development is that adults generally do not like to believe/admit that children have sexual thoughts. But again, I know people who did not have any, and people who wanted to have sex ever they were even 5 years old. It’s just a social taboo to talk about it. Moreover, people have a tendency to deny that they ever had sexual thoughts about a family member, or any behavior that seems “deviant” from the norm. And it is hard to admit to and talk about it because we all want to be what is considered 'normal'.

Moreover, the way I make sense of the world the ego, super ego and Id make perfect sense. Again, as humans we are too arrogant and feel too out of control and helpless when it's even suggested that our personalities and every decision that we make could actually stem from our Id and ego, that are not our conscious decisions and processes. Our sub consciousness can be exactly what makes us who we are, and could account for the decisions that we make. It’s scary, and it makes us feel our of control, so again, that’s a reason enough to disregard it.  

I have another theory, that how we make sense of our world, what we like, what we do, what we say, and most importantly how we think it's determined by a great part by our subconsciousness. Looking at memory, we remember things by associations. And the associations depend on the strength of the association (what we consider important so our values and believes that depend upon our personalities), our experiences, and the recency of the association. Suppose that we see a knife, and the way we each make sense of a knife is different. Some associate it with colors, most with cutting food, some with opening letters, and some with using the knife as a tool to hurt someone/themselves. And I believe the associations we make I believe are based upon our subconsciousness, as our subconciousness has certain drives and needs and places certain importance on certain values and beliefs.

The reason I started understanding and believing Freud’s theories more and more, is because I’ve encountered people who are classic examples of what Freud tried to illustrate. I have met a few people that experience the doctrine of duality in their everyday life. They struggle on daily bases with who they are, and who their subconciousness wants them to be. Imagine that you’re a person who has contradicting needs and thoughts, who needs to actively control their ID everyday in order to be the person they want to be. Imagine being in a relationship with a person that you love more than anything on this planet and at the same time having extremely strong urges to procreate with others than their partner. Imagine being a person that is constantly pulled by two opposite sides regarding practically every decision in their life. And you can’t silence the subconciousness and its drives because it constantly pushes its will through your dreams and thoughts.

So what if we could actually cure that? Cognitive psychology purely fails in many psychological cases. Cognitive psychology fails at many levels, even with curing depression. After years of various cognitive therapies no significant changes are usually found, its just that usually depressed people are told that there is the only way to cure depression and it must help, more of a placebo effect or just purely the feeling of being fed up with therapists and finally giving up.

Purely theoretically, if a man snaps, rapes and then kills his mother, he is labelled in our society as insane. What if he was stuck in a phallic stage, couldn’t help it because his subconciousness dictated his thoughts and eventually his super-ego couldn't suppress his ID he ended up raping and killing her. And this is not meant as an excuse for people who commit such atrocities, but what if we were able to help them prior to the murder? What if really through psychodynamics and catharsis we can help also for example some smokers, excessive eaters or alcoholics who actually are just fixated on the oral stage? What if instead of saying that serial cheaters are just like that because they love sex, what if they want a long term meaningful relationship with their partner but cannot stop cheating because they are fixated in the phallic stage?

So why was psychodynamics thrown out the trash? The research apparently disproving psychodynamics is faulty as assumes that everyone is fixated at a stage, but that's incorrect. I would urge more constructive discussion on the matter and research. I see a lot of potential applications of Freud's psychodynamics. My SO and I had been together for seven years, had two kids together, and I loved them more than I can even put in to words. The relationship had lasted basically my whole adult life and I really considered them to be a part of me, much like a limb.

I cheated on them and they wanted to leave for the past couple years. I talked them in to staying and trying to fix things, but numerous efforts didn't work. I finally gave up and we split. Fortunately events that transpired during our short separation (a story for another time) caused us to get back together and move past the cheating.

So I can speak to the short term feelings of it being over for a couple weeks and the long term of them openly being done for two years.

The first was honestly more of a relief than anything. I was devastated and more unhappy than I could articulate, certainly, but there was also relief at the sense of abandoning a lost cause and hope that we could at least build a friendship and be good parents.

The latter case on the other hand was much worse. I've never being through as much pain and sadness as hearing my love say they don't love me and just want to move on. I cried and drank a lot when I was forced to confront it but mostly just was in denial ("they just said that in anger; they don't really mean it.").

Had we not gotten back together I don't think I'd have ever recovered. While I'd made a FWB during the time we were apart, I don't think I'd have ever had another serious relationship again. Life would have just been work, parenting, and the occasional bit of fun with my friend.
